title: Menopause — symptoms
claims: A change in the normal pattern of periods, such as periods becoming irregular, is usually but not always the first sign of perimenopause.
Common mental health symptoms include low mood, anxiety, mood swings, low self-esteem and problems with memory or concentration (brain fog).

Common physical symptoms include hot flushes with sudden feelings of hot or cold in the face, neck and chest that can cause dizziness; difficulty sleeping; palpitations; headaches and migraines that are worse than usual; muscle aches and joint pains; changed body shape and weight gain; dry and itchy skin; reduced sex drive; vaginal dryness and pain; recurrent urinary tract infections; and sensitive teeth or painful gums.
Symptoms can last for months or years and can change with time; joint pain and vaginal dryness can carry on after periods stop.
The NHS advises seeing a GP or nurse if you think you have perimenopause or menopause symptoms.
Hormonal contraception can affect periods and may mask or control menopausal symptoms, making it hard to know when menopause has been reached.
